sources.coverage: Search: billiard cushion, pool rail, felt roll, chalk cue, rack scrape, pocket drop, ball return, bar ambience, crowd walla, footsteps, chair scrape. Prefer original field recordings and CC0 or CC BY. Reject NC and ND material. This listing specifies noncommercial use. Audio acceptance: dry isolated cues, multiple strengths and variants; avoid speech/music baked into one-shots. Maintain distinct cue-ball impact, ball-ball impact, rail hit, pocket drop, chute, rolling loop, chalk scrape, rack movement, ball placement, miscue, jump/landing, room tone and feedback sounds. Drive volume from collision energy, pitch variation within realistic limits, panning from location; avoid triggering sounds every physics tick. Preserve WAV source; encode compact browser runtime copies. Do not claim that every required sound has a verified dedicated recording yet.

sources.title: Khronos glTF Sample Assets
sources.coverage: Technical reference or software; not a redistributable game asset by default. Use to validate GLB loader, PBR, clearcoat, compression, and animation support; individual sample model licenses vary. Do not bulk import as game content. Physics acceptance: generic rigid-body physics alone is not proof of accurate billiards. Test translational/angular coupling, slide-to-roll, rolling friction, spin decay, restitution, throw, cushion spin response, high-speed tunneling, pocket jaw geometry, simultaneous collisions, realistic breaks, cue offset, cue elevation, jump/massé (if included), deterministic replay and stable resting states. Separate the visual model from collision geometry. Calibrate against published properties and reference shots, not arbitrary game-feel constants. 10 | AGENT ACQUISITION AND INTEGRATION CONTRACT 1. Inspect the existing Euclidi Games asset folder before downloading. Deduplicate by source URL, source ID and SHA-256. Reuse compatible existing assets first. 2. Read source page and archive license. Capture source URL, author, license version, access date, filename and required attribution. If terms are missing or conflict, quarantine metadata only. Do not bypass logins or paywalls. 3. Fetch P0 art and audio in priority order. Use source pages or official APIs, avoid blind recursive mirrors and third-party download wrappers. Respect API limits, site terms and practical storage limits. Preserve source files only where redistribution is explicitly allowed. Where it is not, keep links only. 4. Open representative models and sounds before bulk import. Record dimensions, material maps, mesh count, UVs, topology, rig, format and quality issues. Compare equipment variants visually and select a coherent family. Do not equate free or high polygon count with quality. Obtain visual benchmark approval before mass custom asset generation or expanding a generated set. 5. Normalize to meters (SI internally), consistent axes, correct pivots and scale. GLB/glTF 2.0 for browser 3D; PNG for pixel assets and alpha; WebP/KTX2 for suitable runtime textures; WAV master, Ogg/MP3 runtime audio; WOFF2 fonts. Preserve per-source licenses on converted files. Only use compression that the actual selected runtime and target browsers support. 6. Retain proper UV-mapped stripes and numbers attached to ball rotations. For a missing ball marking or exact collision sphere, procedural generation is justified by geometry/physics requirements. Do not substitute basic shapes for complex table furniture, cushions, pockets, cues or player models. 7. Build a coverage ledger: REQUIRED / AVAILABLE / IMPORTED / TESTED / MISSING. Do not mark assets tested from a search result. Test with actual scene lighting, runtime importer and touch/desktop camera distances. 8. Add P1 assets selectively and P2 only where planned scope needs them. Keep original sources separate from optimized runtime assets. Do not place all high-resolution source archives in the public Pages build. Record size budgets; avoid unnecessary Git history growth and duplicated variants. 9. Generate credits and a machine-readable inventory. For CC BY, record creator, title if supplied, source, license URL and indication of changes; preserve other required notices. For CC0, keep provenance even though attribution is generally not required. Keep code licenses separate from art licenses. 10. Verify catalog entries and deploy only when the actual approved game is implemented and tested; the asset manifest itself authorizes no deployment. Suggested logical asset structure (adapt to the actual repository conventions): assets/billiards/source/equipment/ assets/billiards/source/materials/ assets/billiards/source/audio/ assets/billiards/runtime/models/tables/ assets/billiards/runtime/models/balls/ assets/billiards/runtime/models/cues/ assets/billiards/runtime/models/accessories/ assets/billiards/runtime/models/environment/ assets/billiards/runtime/materials/ assets/billiards/runtime/hdris/ assets/billiards/runtime/sprites/ assets/billiards/runtime/audio/sfx/ assets/billiards/runtime/audio/ambience/ assets/billiards/runtime/audio/music/ assets/billiards/runtime/ui/ assets/billiards/runtime/fonts/ assets/billiards/metadata/manifest.json assets/billiards/metadata/LICENSES.txt assets/billiards/metadata/credits.txt assets/billiards/metadata/coverage.csv Reference documents/code links outside runtime assets. Recommended inventory fields: asset_id, category, variant, priority, title, creator, source_url, license_id, license_url, attribution_text, retrieved_date, source_filename, sha256, local_source_path, runtime_path, format, bytes, dimensions_m, triangles, texture_resolution, dependencies, modifications, validation_status, notes. 11 | COVERAGE GAPS TO RESOLVE BEFORE CLAIMING ASSET COMPLETENESS accurate snooker/carom/blackball variants.
